Umbilical Hernia

Develops at or near the belly button. Often treated with minimally invasive keyhole procedures with or without mesh depending on the size of the defect.

Primary Technique: IPOM/Open Anesthesia: General/Spinal

Surgical Scar

Incisional Hernia

Primary Technique: TAR/eTEP Anesthesia: General
Book Consultation
Abdominal Wall

Ventral Hernia

Develops anywhere along the midline of the abdominal wall. Often treated laparoscopically to ensure minimal postoperative pain and lower recurrence rate.

Primary Technique: eTEP/IPOM Anesthesia: General
Book Consultation
Belly Button Area

Paraumbilical Hernia

Occurs just above or below the umbilicus, often in adults under physical stress. Daycare surgical repair is highly effective and allows same-day discharge.

Primary Technique: Laparoscopic/Open Anesthesia: General/Spinal

Surgical Approaches

Hernia Surgery Options

Modern hernia surgery utilizes several approaches. Dr. Kumar will recommend the most appropriate procedure based on your anatomy, hernia size, and medical history.

Advanced Technology

Laparoscopic & Robotic

An innovative, keyhole technique utilizing small incisions (0.5 to 1 cm) where a miniature camera guides the surgeon. Micro-instruments or robotic arms place the medical mesh behind the defect with extreme accuracy, avoiding muscle cutting and reducing surgical trauma.

✓ Significantly reduced postoperative pain
✓ Minimal scarring & premium cosmetic results
✓ Preferred for bilateral & recurrent hernias
✓ Rapid recovery and return to work
⏱️ Recovery: 1 to 3 weeks. Often discharged as a daycare procedure on the same day.
Traditional Surgery

Open Hernia Repair

A classic surgical method where a single incision is made near the hernia bulge. The surgeon gently pushes the protruding tissue back into place and secures the abdominal wall defect with sutures. Medical mesh is typically applied to reinforce the weakened region and prevent recurrence.

✓ Best for complex or incarcerated hernias
✓ Local or regional anesthesia options
✓ Time-tested surgical reliability
✓ Cost-effective procedural path
⏱️

Open vs. Laparoscopic Comparison

Feature Open Surgery Laparoscopic / Robotic
Incision Size 3 to 6 inches (single incision) 3 keyholes (0.5 to 1 cm each)
Hospital Stay 1-3 days typically Often same-day discharge (daycare)
Pain Level Moderate to significant Minimal to mild
Recovery Time 3-6 weeks 1-3 weeks
Best Suited For Extremely large, complicated, or obstructed hernias Primary ventral, groin, bilateral repairs
Medical Necessity

When is Hernia Surgery Recommended?

Not all hernias warrant emergency surgery, but because hernias cannot heal on their own, surgical repair is the only definitive cure. Dr. Kumar determines the timing of intervention based on clinical severity.

Emergency Indicators

Elective Surgery

Recommended for symptomatic hernias causing pain or heavy sensations during standing/lifting, to prevent progressive wall enlargement and reduce risk of future strangulation.

Watchful Waiting

Small, completely asymptomatic hernias might be observed under strict professional guidance. Dr. Kumar will review the risks of delay during consultation.

Post-Surgery

Surgical Recovery Timeline

Modern laparoscopic and robotic repair techniques accelerate healing times. Here is what to anticipate during your post-op window.

1
Immediate

First 24 Hours

You will rest in the post-op recovery suite. Pain management plans will be initiated. Most laparoscopic patients are ambulatory and walk within hours of surgery.

2
Days 1-7

First Week at Home

Prioritize light home walks. Keep surgical dressings dry as instructed. Avoid driving, heavy abdominal straining, or lifting objects exceeding 5 kg. Desk work can often be restarted.

3
Weeks 2-4

Gradual Activity Progression

Introduce gentle cardiovascular exercises like outdoor walking or stationary cycling. Avoid core-straining abdominal workouts or intense weight-lifting routines.

4
Weeks 6-8

Full Recovery Achieved

Standard tissue healing is complete. Patients can resume high-intensity gym sessions, heavy weights, and athletic sports. Scheduled follow-up reviews ensure optimal long-term outcomes.

🤷‍♂️ FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

Yes, in the vast majority of adult hernia repairs, a medical-grade mesh is used. Medical studies show that using mesh reduces the risk of the hernia returning (recurrence rate) to less than 1-2%, compared to over 20-30% when closed with stitches alone.

Standard hernia repairs typically take between 30 to 90 minutes. Most laparoscopic and robotic groin and umbilical hernia repairs are performed as daycare (same-day) procedures, allowing you to return home on the same day once you have fully recovered from anesthesia.

For laparoscopic or robotic repairs, patients can often return to desk jobs in 3-7 days and light cardiovascular exercise in 2 weeks. For open surgeries, it may take 1-2 weeks for desk work. In both cases, lifting objects heavier than 5 kg and intense abdominal training should be avoided for 4 to 6 weeks.
